newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares shunned Wall Street's rich overnight gains to trade weaker on Friday morning before being pulled higher by futures trade to finish strong, dealers said.
They said that the South African market was exceptionally volatile at the moment because it as dominated by futures-related trade, which could knock shares down or build them up at will.
In early trade industrials were dragged down by futures players and not even a strong close on Wall Street could buoy them, but in afternoon trade futures-related trade pushed industrials up.

"Industrials finished th day reasonably firm. In teh morning theyvwere knocked down on futures selling, then they kicked back up and were probably pushed by futures trade again. There was some big futures arbitrage going on," one dealer said.
"Industrials are likely to remain this voaltile as long as thir trade is linked to futures," he added.
Industrials finished the day 40.7 points higher at 8,003.3.
At the start the equity futures market was puzzled by slight weakness all round despite an overnight surge on Wall Street.
Dealers attributed it to a slide in bullion price which was depressing gold futures and could be weighing on all contracts.
They also said that many players were long with no room to buy and their nerves were now on edge.
But futures players managed to keep their grip by manipulating the cash market and most contracts finished steady to slightly firmer.
The March all-share contract stood at 6,103/15 from 6,081 on Thursday, the industrial contract was at 7,772/77 from 7,764 close and gold contract is at 940/60 from a 958 close.
